Stumps on day 4 = 18:03 local, 16:03 GMT, 21:33 IST: Phewf! How do you describe that? Test cricket never fails to amaze us. Just when you think, there's no life left, you would often see resurrection through a fiery spell or a stubborn knock. And when two batters combine to breathe new life and bring back balance into the contest, it's gotta be extra special. Been that kinda day for Ryan Rickelton and Wiaan Mulder who both played the finest innings of their international career thus far. The day started off with a lead of 40 with 6 wickets in the bank and an all-out inside two sessions looked inevitable. Not to be. While Rickelton engineered a 50-run stand with Breetzke, he then joined hands with Mulder to notch up the most valuable partnership of this series. The pair added 154 for the 6th wicket and the most impressive bit about their assocation was that they barely gave any sniff to their opposition.

So solid was the duo, it needed a brilliant fielding effort from Inglis to pull curtains on their partnership. Once Rickelton fell, the hosts lost their next 3 wickets for 16 runs. Mulder was on 82 when number 11, Rabada, walked out to bat. The all-rounder then took things into his control and only exposed Rabada for a maximum of 2 balls per over. Eventually, he claimed his 4th Test ton and never lost patience despite the drought of boundaries. Skill. Character. Grit - You name it, and the home team had every answer to the Aussies. They did it all with no fuss. That said, Australia tried hard but their bowling wasn't as incisive and consistent as it was yesterday. And therefore, find themselves chasing 288 on a surface that seem to have a few tricks for the spinners. Can Harmer and Co. back it up tomorrow? Travis Head to belt a hundred before lunch? What predictions have you got? Join us early tomorrow for what promises to be a fitting final day of the series. Cheers!!

15:20 Local Time, 13:20 GMT, 18:50 IST: March 2023 was the last time Australia lost a Test series. They've been a great team under Cummins, winning the WTC in 2023, and then making the final in 2025. But their bowling attack isn't getting any younger, their batting seems to be in disarray, and they've been beaten by the better team over the last couple of weeks. After a sensational win in Gqeberha to level the series, South Africa have registered yet another remarkable come-from-behind win here in Cape Town. Today it was set up to be a humdinger with Australia needing 288 in the fourth innings, and South Africa needing 10 wickets. There was such excitement about all the posibilities of a close contest. But it turned out to be an anticlimax with the match being decided in the first session thanks to a procession of wickets from Rabada and Harmer.

Quite remarkable how Test cricket has so many life lessons tucked into it. On the opening morning, Pat Cummins' decision to bowl first on a flat deck came under scrutiny as South Africa's batters made the Australian attack look ordinary. Yet, by the end of the day, Australia had turned things around spectacularly, claiming the last four wickets for just two runs. Their batters carried that momentum forward, with five of the top six getting past 40. Josh Inglis, stepping in for the injured Steve Smith, ensured the absence of Australia's premier Test batter wasn't felt, producing a magnificent century. A handy 100-run lead followed, and by the close of Day 3, South Africa were effectively 40/4 in their second innings, with the game firmly in the balance.

Facing a must-win situation on Day 4, the hosts responded in style through magnificent centuries from Ryan Rickelton and Wiaan Mulder. Their match-defining 154-run stand for the sixth wicket helped South Africa set Australia a daunting target of 288. Both sides would have fancied their chances heading into the final day, but only one managed to turn belief into action. Kagiso Rabada, who had been laid low by illness on Days 2 and 3, returned with a vengeance, striking twice in the opening over before removing Australia's biggest hope, Travis Head, six overs later. From there, Simon Harmer tightened the screws with a web of spin, finishing with a well-deserved maiden ten wicket haul in the game. South Africa eventually stormed to a memorable 176-run victory, clinching the series 2-1 and reclaiming the No. 1 spot in Test cricket. All in all, a terrific series in which both sides fought tooth and nail. Stick around for the post-match reactions!

South Africa, under Bavuma, continue to achieve incredible things. Down 0-1 in the series, they've gone on to produce two of the greatest comeback wins in consecutive Tests to take the series along with the No. 1 Test ranking. The trophy is theirs and Bavuma takes it to his teammates as they pose for the photos with the Table Mountain in the backdrop. As for Australia, there has already been a lot of debate over some of the choices that were made this week, including the decision to leave out Scott Boland and particularly the decision to bowl first. A stunning second new ball spell from Mitchell Starc raised hopes of getting them out of jail but it wasn't to be. Their batting remains a major concern and after the exclusion of Nic Maddinson, there are now big question marks about the future of Marnus Labuschagne. Their bowling attack isn't getting any younger either. Will be interesting to see what they do when New Zealand come touring in December.

So that's all from this series which many feel should've been four or five Tests long. But we take what we get, and what we got was a lot of fun. Hope you enjoyed our coverage. It's a goodbye from Sagar Chawla on behalf of Praveen Kumar and Raju Peethala!
